title: The Dumaine band lineup and trombonists Yank and Dusen
summary: Band lineup on the records; Yank played Ory-style slide trombone; Dusen used vowels.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah. So, uh, Earl, uh, Humphrey was trombone, was he? No. In the band? Yeah, Earl. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

On the band? On the band? Yeah, yeah, yeah. On the band? On the band, yeah. Well, and, uh, Clash Gabriel was on the guitar, wasn't it? I think. And Willie LaBeff was on drums. And, uh, this boy Yank, I think, was on trombone. No, Earl was on trombone, yeah. Uh, trombone, yeah. Uh, Yank used to play with us too, you know, from Al Jase. Which band? Whose band? He used to play with the Lewiston man. The Louis Dumaine, what do you think? Louis Dumaine. Yeah, yeah, yeah. And, uh... How did Yank play? Oh, yeah.
I don't think he made any records. What kind of a style did he have? Was he something like Deucin or like Ory or who?

Well, he's something like Ory. He's a wonderful trombone player. Really a good drummer. Yeah, oh yeah. He could hit that lead, you know. He could hit, he could lead on the trombone. Yeah, he could play the melodies, huh? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Would you say that he played a sort of a vamp style, it's all did he? Bamper to the blues.
No, no. He just, he just played that real sliding trombone music. You know what I mean? A kind of strength. Yeah, strength, yeah. Did he use the sliding trombone?
He didn't use the vowels. No, no, no.

Frankie Duesen used to use the vowels. I don't remember Jack Carey using the vowels. I think he used the slides. Slides, too. But Frankie Duesen was a vowel trombone player, you know. And my uncle also. And used to be people coming from New Orleans, the typical, this year my uncle played trombone. Oh, we had one, eleven, twelve o'clock at night, you could do every instrument in the band, you know. That's pretty. Yeah. Yeah. Yes sir. We had a real string band.
